articles.title: Rachel Zegler, Aaron Sorkin, Bradley Whitford, Diego Rodriguez Announced as Speakers at Variety’s Business of Broadway Breakfast
articles.summary: Variety has announced programming for its annual Business of Broadway Breakfast, presented by City National Bank. The program, on Oct. 5 in New York City, will feature Rachel Zegler, Aaron Sorkin, Bradley Whitford and Diego Rodriguez.
body: The program will include a producers panel featuring Amanda Lipitz, Haley Swindal, Susan Kelechi Watson, and Brian Lee. Business of Broadway is sponsored by City National Bank and will be hosted by Tom Felton.

The day’s final keynote will feature the cast and crew of “Dolly: A True Original Musical,” opening at the St. James Theater on Jan. 19, on what would have been Dolly Parton’s 81st birthday. Producer Adam Speers, director Bartlett Sherr and the cast bring Dolly Parton and Maria S. Schlatter’s book to life following Dolly from Tennessee to the bright lights of Hollywood.

The Producers Panel will feature Amanda Lipitz (“Galileo”), Haley Swindal (“Damn Yankees”), Susan Kelechi Watson (“School Girls; Or, The African Mean Girls Play”) and Brian Lee (“Awake and Sing!” and “Here There Are Blueberries”). The panel will be moderated by Erik Piecuch, Senior VP/team leader of entertainment & sports banking at City National Bank.
Variety will also feature the individuals profiled in its 10 Broadway to Watch list, published on Sept. 30, presented by City National Bank.

articles.title: ‘He made something every single day’: David Lynch’s inscrutable photography celebrated in LA show
articles.summary: The director’s surrealist films defined Los Angeles. Now the city is celebrating his other passion: photography. No one can bring Los Angeles together like David Lynch.
body: The first posthumous exhibition of the director and artist’s photographs went on display at LA’s Pace Gallery this weekend, drawing a massive crowd of goths, weirdos and art world observers to celebrate a creative mind that has few equals in American pop culture history.

Lynch’s disappearance from this mortal plane last year has not dimmed the public’s appreciation for his surrealist, idiosyncratic perspective on American life. The exhibition – featuring photos that are erotic, disturbing and sometimes comically violent – encapsulates all the things that made Lynch one of the city’s foremost creative minds.

Photos of mysterious women blowing smoke, multiple exposures of a nude subject on a chaise longue, dissected animals; the work is “radical”, said Bill Griffin, managing partner for Pace Gallery. “It dealt with the human condition in a very large way. It dealt with consciousness and unconsciousness.” Pace represented Lynch for years, and is spearheading the efforts to maintain and catalogue his fine art work with the David Lynch Foundation.
points: Now the city is celebrating his other passion: photography.
No one can bring Los Angeles together like David Lynch.

articles.title: Dick Guttman, Renowned Hollywood Publicist to Stars Including Barbra Streisand and Clint Eastwood, Dies at 93
articles.summary: Dick Guttman, the longtime Hollywood publicity executive and screenwriter who worked with clients including Barbra Streisand, Clint Eastwood and many more, died Sept. 19 in Los Altos, Calif. He was 93.
body: While attending UCLA, he worked part-time for Rogers & Cowan PR, then became a unit publicist in Europe, where he worked on films including “Paris Holiday” and “The Key.” He met his wife Gisela while in Paris as unit publicist on Billy Wilder’s “Love in the Afternoon,” and they married in 1956.

When Guttman returned to Los Angeles, he worked at Rogers & Cowan for more than a decade, representing top actors at the time when actors weren’t under contract to studios and “press agents,” in his preferred terminology, became pivotal to successful careers.

He partnered with Jerry Pam in 1971 to form Guttman & Pam, which became one of Hollywood’s top agencies over two decades. Guttman formed his own agency, Guttman Associates, in the early 1990s, repping dozens of top stars as well as promoting films such as “Unforgiven,” “Dirty Harry,” “Bonnie and Clyde,” “The Conversation,” “Kramer vs. Kramer,” “All That Jazz,” “The Year of Living Dangerously,” “The Man Who Would Be King,” “The King’s Speech,” “The Artist,” “Shakespeare in Love and “The English Patient.”
Guttman Associates continues to represent Hollywood talent with Guttman’s colleagues Susan Madore and Rona Menashe overseeing the firm.

articles.title: CNN Chief Says He’s ‘Enthusiastic’ About Staying Under Paramount, but Not Sure He Can
articles.summary: CNN’s top executive told staffers Wednesday that he wants to stay at the news giant, but has little knowledge of what the outlet’s soon-to-be new corporate parent has in store.
body: The meeting was scheduled several days ago and not because of Paramount’s victory this week, according to a person familiar with the matter. CNN declined to make executives available for comment. Thompson also told staffers, in response to a question posed by veteran correspondent John King, that he did not know when a transition might start or when Paramount executives might be seen in CNN’s officers.
Thompson cautioned staffers that it was not clear that Paramount intended to merge CNN and CBS News, but had no detail to offer about what next steps might look like under the new owner.

During his tenure, Thompson has focused on getting CNN content in front of younger viewers and digital audiences. CNN has been testing new formats with its “CNN All Access” subscription service, and has seen up and coming personnel like Abby Phillip and Harry Enten gain some traction. Warner Bros. Discovery projected in a filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission earlier this year that CNN will generate $600 million in profit in 2026 on $1.8 billion in revenue.

articles.title: Jeffrey Katzenberg Says Hollywood Must Accept AI as a Tool: It ‘Is Not Going Away’
articles.summary: Jeffrey Katzenberg, the legendary Hollywood producer and executive, thinks the entertainment industry needs to accept AI if it wants to remain relevant. In a 2,377-word essay posted to X on Wednesday, Katzenberg leaned on his history working through the industry’s various technological changes.
body: The essay follows the yearslong debate over AI’s place within the creative industry, which has further rankled people after AI company leaders acknowledged the tools may slip out of human control.

Katzenberg’s WndrCo recently invested in Reactor, a startup that says its platform can produce gen-AI video in real time. About Reactor, he told Variety, “I was incredibly impressed, if not astounded, by just how innovative their approach is to storytelling tools.” Katzenberg also has reportedly discussed creating a new AI video startup with the former head of OpenAI’s now-defunct Sora.
“The tools-versus-no-tools argument is a trap,” he wrote. “First, we must all agree that there should be terms. Then we can have the crucial debate about what fairness requires.”

Once those terms are decided upon and agreed to by all creative stakeholders, Katzenberg thinks it could lead to a new Hollywood renaissance — though he admitted he didn’t have all the answers. “How we come through this is a choice,” he wrote.

articles.title: Boorman and the Devil review – enjoyable re-evaluation of the disaster that was Exorcist II: The Heretic
articles.summary: John Boorman generously details the mortifying experience of making a sequel to 1973 hit horror The Exorcist, which was widely and unfairly panned. David Kittredge gives us a thoroughly enjoyable, detailed account of the catastrophe that was John Boorman’s 1977 film Exorcist II: The Heretic, the…
body: According to an apocryphal tale gleefully repeated by William Friedkin, director of the first film, the sequel resulted in an enraged audience one night turning round and booing Warner Brothers executives in the back row of the cinema, and then chasing them out of the building and down the street. Boorman desperately recut the film with the sillier bits removed. But the damage was done.

Boorman is interviewed here and generously goes into great detail about his painful and mortifying experience with the film, how he had originally been offered the first Exorcist, disliked the story and turned it down, but was induced to take on the sequel. Perhaps Kittredge could have made it clearer how risky it was for Boorman to have taken on a project which he fundamentally didn’t believe in and was somehow creatively working against. He hired a kind of script-and-direction consultant, his friend Rospo Pallenberg, whose influence with Boorman annoyed the cast.
points: John Boorman generously details the mortifying experience of making a sequel to 1973 hit horror The Exorcist, which was widely and unfairly panned.

articles.title: Harvey Weinstein sentenced to 15 years in prison for sexual assault
articles.summary: Assault survivor Miriam Haley said the "devastating effect on my life and sense of security that may never go away".
body: Disgraced Hollywood producer Harvey Weinstein has been sentenced to 15 years in prison, after a jury found him guilty last year of committing a criminal sexual act against a former assistant.
Appearing in court in a wheelchair, Weinstein denied the allegations but apologised to "anyone I may have hurt by my actions".
Weinstein has already spent several years jailed in New York, where he has faced three trials over rape and abuse allegations. He was convicted in a seperate sex-crime case in Los Angeles.

This is the second time he has been given a prison sentence in the Miriam Haley case. Weinstein was first convicted and sentenced in 2020, but New York's highest court overturned the conviction in 2024, along with another involving actress Jessica Mann. The court ruled that Weinstein did not get a fair trial.
points: Assault survivor Miriam Haley said the "devastating effect on my life and sense of security that may never go away".

articles.title: North Sea, Nature Untamed review – stunning footage finds the beauty and splendour under the water
articles.summary: Diver Peter van Rodijnen’s footage of basking whales, plankton blooms and fatherly fish disputes the idea that the North Sea is a bleak wilderness. The North Sea, with its cold grey waters, is the world’s drabbest.
body: First, the greyness. Van Rodijnen films the North Sea’s waves sparkling with the cosmic blue light of bioluminescent algae, and lit up with the disco colours of coral and plankton blooms. He also brings us cute, coo-worthy stories from the depths; take the male shorthorn sculpin fish (no looker, it must be said) who spends the winter looking after his eggs, cleaning and blowing fresh water over them. Van Rodijnen’s camera is there for the baby fish hatching – pop, pop, pop out of their pearly plump pink eggs. There are some quirky stories, too, including a barnacle with a superlong penis.

articles.title: Netherlands to return to Eurovision after 2026 boycott
articles.summary: The country did not participate in this year's contest but will return next year in Bulgaria.
body: The Netherlands will return to the Eurovision Song Contest next year despite a boycott by the broadcaster that was previously in charge of the country's participation.

Dutch network Avrotros withdrew in 2026 and said it would also not take part in 2027 because the competition could "no longer be considered neutral" given divisions over Israel's involvement and the Gaza war.

The NPO, which oversees public broadcasting in the country, has now stepped in, saying coverage of the contest will be provided by broadcasting organisation NOS, while an independent panel will select the Dutch participant.
Jurre Bosman, NPO's director of media, said: "It is important that, as a public broadcaster, we remain part of this unifying European event at this moment in particular."

articles.title: Singer Michael Kiwanuka reveals he is recovering from a stroke
articles.summary: The award-winning musician says he faces a "tough journey ahead" after a "quite severe" brain injury.
body: Award-winning singer-songwriter Michael Kiwanuka has revealed he has suffered a stroke and faces a "long, tough journey ahead" to recover.

The 39-year-old from London, who won the Mercury Prize in 2020 and has been nominated for five Brit Awards, said in an Instagram post that the stroke occurred "a few months ago" and was caused "by a bleed in my brain brought on by high blood pressure".
He added that "the brain injury I suffered was quite severe so there's a lot of rehab to be done", but told fans he will "look forward to seeing you all soon".
Kiwanuka simultaneously announced the release of his fifth album, titled Fudge, which was recorded before the stroke.

articles.summary: Before Anthony Hopkins’ Dr Lecter in The Silence of the Lambs, Brian Cox played a cannibalistic killer in Mann’s pioneering Red Dragon adaptation. Five years before The Silence of the Lambs, there was writer-director Michael Mann’s pioneering Thomas Harris adaptation Manhunter, now on re-release in…
body: After the trauma and burnout of tracking down Lecktor, Graham has been persuaded back on to the job by FBI chief Jack Crawford (Dennis Farina), desperate for his expert help; this has obvious implications for what no one in 1986 called Graham’s “mental health”. Graham is brilliant at the job because he can think his way into the serial killer’s twisted mind, and doing this all over again could send him over the edge. Right now, he has a very 80s-looking luxury sunkissed beachfront home in Florida in which to spend his retirement.

The Tooth Fairy himself is Francis Dollarhyde (Tom Noonan) who has a Frankenstein’s-monster type tendresse with a blind co-worker called Reba, played by Joan Allen. It is with her that the film has the strange and rather amazing, if preposterous, scene; somehow Dollarhyde has connections at the zoo which lets him get Reba in behind the scenes to stroke a sedated tiger in one of the most startling “first date” scenes in cinema.
